summary: Iteration 110 — Sprint 2 consolidation regression testing PASSED. All 17 pytest cases green (auth for admin/client/specialist, settings façade with dual-write, security_config via settings_store, /api/public/demo-request → unified `leads` with AI triage, /api/interior-design/assistant AI chat with session_id, XOS registry + experience-profiles for all 3 roles, health). Frontend regression PASSED: landing page loads cleanly with CMS-driven SiteNav (Acasă/Servicii/Pentru Proprietari/Companie/Cont), admin login + XOS Builder renders both XOSRegistryPanel and ExperienceProfilesPanel (iter109 bug is confirmed FIXED — 3 exp-save-* buttons present), client login lands on /client dashboard with properties + active jobs + Copilot, public demo-request form E2E submits successfully → success dialog «Mulțumim!» → lead written to legacy demo_leads AND unified leads collection with triage (score:40, segment:nurture, source:demo, meta.legacy_id set). Dual-write verified for settings (company.tagline mirrored to app_settings legacy) and leads. AI chat responded < 15s with session_id echoed back. No regressions detected from Sprint 2 backend consolidation.

minor.issue: Not gated by security_guard/rate_limit — accepts anonymous requests. Not a regression, but worth noting since Emergent LLM credits are consumed per call. Existing rate limiter only applies to /concierge paths.

action_items: Update /app/memory/test_credentials.md: admin password shown as 'Admin123!' but actual seeded password from backend/.env SEED_ADMIN_PASSWORD is '1!nasov01ADMIN'. Doc drift causes future testers to fail admin login. Either sync SEED_ADMIN_PASSWORD to Admin123! (seed.py updates existing admin idempotently) or update the doc.
critical_code_review_comments: settings_store.py get_settings falls back to legacy correctly, but strips '_id' + 'key' — good. However `security_config` legacy filter is {"_id": "global"} while _save_config writes via patch_settings which triggers legacy dual-write with $set on the same doc. Verified working (security config test passed). No issue.

public.py demo-request line 46 idempotency check uses regex `^{day}` on `created_at` string — safe, but for very active hours multiple entries per email/day still collapse to 1 lead. Acceptable business logic.

leads_store.py _triage: score cap 100, phone adds +20, budget adds +15/+25, notes>60 chars adds +10. Test lead had all criteria BUT the message field maps to `notes` legacy field? Actually demo_leads stores under `message` not `notes` — `_triage` reads `root['notes']` or `meta['message']`; meta contains message so length check works. Confirmed score=40 (base 20 + notes 10 + budget 0 + company 10). Correct.

ai_session_store.py sync_all is periodic (every 30 min per Sprint 2.3 spec) — interior_design chat writes to legacy interior_assistant_sessions; sync fires later. Fine for MVP but any test looking for immediate visibility in ai_sessions after a chat must wait or call sync_all manually.

app_settings.py update_settings line 199-202 dual-writes to settings_store 'app' namespace inside try/except that swallows exceptions with `pass` (no log) — if settings_store breaks silently we'd never know. Add logger.warning.
public.py line 46 async DB scan `demo_leads.find({email, created_at regex})` without index on (email, created_at) — fine for demo volumes; add compound index if traffic grows.
interior_design.py /interior-design/assistant is unauth + unguarded — abuse can drain LLM credits. Consider adding security_guard dependency or IP rate limit.

Log during startup: 'Resend send failed: The associated domain with your API key is not verified' — not a Sprint 2 issue, pre-existing email deliverability problem. Admin notifications for new demo leads will silently fail.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (landing + admin XOS panels + client dashboard + demo E2E all PASS)
